Description - SavePlaylist

Saves the player's playlist to the account. A playlist is an ordinary folder named after the playlist, created inside a top-level folder Playlisty, which the server creates at the account root when missing (parentId is its id). There is no parent parameter. The listed files are copied into the playlist folder under new file ids (Download/playlist-folder-listing). The playlist folder came back with a server-generated password value while passwd=false (Folders/playlist-folder). It is removed like any folder (RemoveFolder/playlist-folder-force).

Verification: verified live in the real-client form (token, name, list, unused id = -1) in guarded runs with full-tree snapshots. An existing Playlisty is reused (same parentId), and a duplicate playlist name becomes a new folder <name>(1) (no space) with status Ok and a fresh copy of the files (duplicate-name-playlisty-exists, Download/playlist-duplicate-listing). Playlisty itself has passwd=true and a server-generated password (Folders/playlisty-after-duplicate, redacted).

When the client sends it: player "save playlist to hamster".

Routing. The path item declares the server http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc?op=, so this operation resolves to http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc?op=/SavePlaylist. WCF ignores the query string and dispatches only on the SOAPAction header (verified live). The real client posts to the bare http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc; both URLs reach the same operation. A path suffix (.svc/SavePlaylist) does not work (a:DestinationUnreachable, see soapRestStylePath).

Wire format. POST with Content-Type: text/xml;charset=utf-8 (exact client bytes, no space; the server answers text/xml; charset=utf-8) and SOAPAction: http://chomikuj.pl/IChomikBoxService/SavePlaylist (unquoted). Body: SOAP 1.1 envelope, UTF-8, no indentation, parameters in the documented order (WCF silently drops out-of-order parameters). The client gzips the body (Content-Encoding: gzip).

Path notes

SOAP operation SavePlaylist. The path-level server makes the URL routable: WCF dispatches on SOAPAction and ignores the ?op=/SavePlaylist query.

Schema

Schema SavePlaylistRequestEnvelope, as an XML element tree in wire order. Namespaces are shown where they change.

  • <s:Envelope> object required SavePlaylistRequestEnvelope xmlns http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/

    SOAP 1.1 request envelope for SavePlaylist: <s:Envelope><s:Body><SavePlaylist xmlns="http://chomikuj.pl/">…. No SOAP header is ever sent; xmlns:i is declared on the operation element only when a nil value is present.

    • @s:encodingStyle string optional = "http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/encoding/" namespace http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/

      SOAP 1.1 encodingStyle attribute. The real client always writes it; the service accepts the envelope with or without it.

    • <s:Body> object required

      Exactly one operation element; no other content (this also makes the per-operation envelopes mutually exclusive).

      • <SavePlaylist> object required SavePlaylistRequest xmlns http://chomikuj.pl/

        Operation element SavePlaylist in http://chomikuj.pl/ (trailing slash is mandatory: with http://chomikuj.pl the parameters are not matched, see Service/wrong-operation-namespace).

        • <token> string required Token

          Session token. Always the first child.

        • <sequence> object optional nullable (i:nil) MessageSequence

          Optional chunk header (server contract); the client does not send it for SavePlaylist.

          • <stamp> string required

            Random correlation value, the same for all parts (a random number generated by the client). The server does not key stored parts by it.

          • <part> integer (int32) required

            Zero-based part index.

          • <count> integer (int32) required

            Total number of parts.

        • <name> string required

          Playlist name.

        • <list> list required

          Playlist items.

          • <PlayListItem> object optional repeated PlayListItem

            One playlist entry. The client sends exactly one real id per item and -1 for the other.

            • <id> integer (int64) required

              File id, or -1.

            • <realId> integer (int64) required

              Real id, or -1: the client sends id when it is > 0, otherwise -1 and realId. Meaning Inferred (the stored file shared by copies); never non-zero live.

Responses - 200, 500

200

SOAP response envelope. HTTP 200 is used for every service-level outcome, including errors: check SavePlaylistResult/status. Compressed (Content-Encoding: gzip) when the request accepts gzip.

Schema text/xml

Schema SavePlaylistResponseEnvelope, as an XML element tree in wire order. Namespaces are shown where they change.

  • <s:Envelope> object required SavePlaylistResponseEnvelope xmlns http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/

    SOAP 1.1 response envelope for SavePlaylist: <s:Envelope><s:Body><SavePlaylistResponse xmlns="http://chomikuj.pl/"><SavePlaylistResult …>.

    • <s:Body> object required

      Exactly one response element; no other content.

      • <SavePlaylistResponse> object required xmlns http://chomikuj.pl/
        • <SavePlaylistResult> object required SavePlaylistResult

          Result element; declares xmlns:i (XML Schema instance, for i:nil) and xmlns:a.

          • <a:status> string required Status xmlns http://chomikuj.pl

            Outcome of the call. The client accepts only Ok; BadToken triggers a re-login, anything else is an error.

            7 values
            • "Ok" Success. The only value the client treats as success.
            • "BadToken" Unknown, logged-out or otherwise invalid token. The client re-authenticates (Auth) once per message (message-relog-count=1) and resends the message with the new token; session-bound messages are dropped.
            • "Forbidden" Auth: user name does not exist. The client shows the credentials dialog.
            • "PermissionError" Auth: wrong password for an existing user. The client shows the credentials dialog.
            • "Error" Generic failure. Usually carries a reason in errorMessage (e.g. EmptyName, NameExistsAtDestination); FolderFiles with an unknown disposition returns Error with errorMessage nil (FolderFiles/invalid-disposition).
            • "NotEmptyOrNotExistsFolder" RemoveFolder with force=false on a folder that contains files, or on an unknown/removed folder id.
            • "WrongDisposition" FolderFiles: the disposition is a known value but not allowed for this call (download).
          • <a:errorMessage> string required nullable (i:nil) ErrorMessage xmlns http://chomikuj.pl

            Error detail for status=Error; nil otherwise.

          • <a:folderId> integer (int32) optional xmlns http://chomikuj.pl

            Id of the new playlist folder (0 on error).

          • <a:folderName> string optional nullable (i:nil) xmlns http://chomikuj.pl

            Name of the playlist folder: the requested name, or <name>(1) when a playlist of that name exists.

          • <a:parentId> integer (int32) optional xmlns http://chomikuj.pl

            Id of the top-level Playlisty folder that holds playlists (created by the server at the account root when missing, reused when present).

          • <a:messageSequence> object optional nullable (i:nil) MessageSequence xmlns http://chomikuj.pl

            Echo of the request sequence; nil when none was sent (the client never sends one).

            • <stamp> string required xmlns http://chomikuj.pl/

              Random correlation value, the same for all parts (a random number generated by the client). The server does not key stored parts by it.

            • <part> integer (int32) required xmlns http://chomikuj.pl/

              Zero-based part index.

            • <count> integer (int32) required xmlns http://chomikuj.pl/

              Total number of parts.

500 SoapFault

WCF SOAP fault (HTTP 500, Content-Type: text/xml; charset=utf-8, not compressed). Possible for every SOAP operation: an empty or malformed body gives a:InternalServiceFault, an undeserialisable value a:DeserializationFailed, an unknown or missing SOAPAction a:ActionNotSupported. Operations with an operation-specific captured fault document it inline instead.

Schema text/xml

Schema SoapFaultEnvelope, as an XML element tree in wire order. Namespaces are shown where they change.

  • <s:Envelope> object required SoapFaultEnvelope xmlns http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/

    SOAP 1.1 fault envelope (HTTP 500, Content-Type: text/xml; charset=utf-8, never gzip-compressed).

    • <s:Body> object required
      • <s:Fault> object required SoapFault

        The fault.

        • <faultcode> string required no namespace

          Qualified fault code with its own namespace declaration on the element: a:InternalServiceFault and a:DeserializationFailed (a = http://schemas.microsoft.com/net/2005/12/windowscommunicationfoundation/dispatcher), a:ActionNotSupported and a:DestinationUnreachable (a = http://schemas.microsoft.com/ws/2005/05/addressing/none).

        • <faultstring> object required no namespace

          Human-readable message. DeserializationFailed names the parameter and CLR type, which is how the contract was established.

          • @xml:lang string required namespace http://www.w3.org/XML/1998/namespace

            Language of the message (en-US).

          • text content string required

            Message text.

Client vs live - discrepancies

Where the client's expected behaviour and the live service disagree, the spec follows the live behaviour (x-discrepancies):

  • Server contract has an optional sequence parameter that the client does not send.
  • The client expects a "playlist folder created/updated"; live the service creates an ordinary folder under the root folder Playlisty (created when missing, reused when present) and copies the files (new ids) instead of referencing them; a duplicate name gets the suffix (1).

Security notes - findings that concern SavePlaylist

  • S-02 Medium Folder passwords are returned in plain text over HTTP: ModifyFolder echoes the new password, Folders lists each folder's password, and the folder created by SavePlaylist gets a server-generated password while passwd=false.

From x-security-notes in the spec. Ratings and scope are explained on Security & privacy.
